title: Greasy's and getting cut by Rex Stewart
summary: After the Rhythm Club, Roy went with Rex Stewart to Greasy's on 129th, where Rex's high B-flat beat him.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You mentioned the Rhythm Club. That was like a place where they strictly had sessions. Right?
We used to have people down there when a new cat was comin' down and wanted to play.

And there was another place where I got wiped out by Rex Stewart called Greasy's, on 129th. I really got wiped out by Rex, you know. I think that's when I first met Smalls. I think I must have been working with Charlie Johnson. Yeah. Oh boy. And you know, Rex like stayed in the house, showed me some of my first riffs, and then... I

had so much respect for him, like I told you before, I really wanted to be like the cat, you know. And he came down, he didn't have his horn, and I was talkin' and displayin' (?) things like they do in New York, like "I'm gonna get you after the show; you just go get your horn," you know. ...(?)... he wanted to hear me! And we started going to the Rhythm Club, but he said, "No, no, let's go down to Greasy's." All right.

So we went down there, and I don't know how the word got around -- before you know it, that joint was like that. So there was Gus Aikin, Red Allen and some other trumpet player, I forget who the hell it was... And we started to play. All of Fletcher's cats in there. They were really... They could get really loaded up on (?). And boy, he'd be playing (?), man. And you'd play, they'd go, "Yeah, Little Jazz! Yeah!" -- you know. And Rex was getting eviller and eviller, and big as day, you know.

So I made the mistake of, you know, like coming in on his chorus, and I screamed like a G. Man, the house fell out, you know! And boy, when he came back, he didn't let them other cats get him, he cut my ass and he hit one of them B-flats... I ain't never heard a B-flat that high and that loud and big in my life! And I start feeling around on my horn, and when I was see what that was, I said, "Uh-oh,"
and I took my horn out and I put it in the case. I told the cats, "You can't play as high as me, and I'm gonna give it up now." Man, I had tears in my eyes looking at him.
